description:
Desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1/2 SDR radios.

A Rust/egui desktop client for openHPSDR Protocol 1 and Protocol 2 radios (Metis/Ozy-style and Hermes/Orion-style boards), using WDSP for DSP.

- Protocol 1 (Metis/Ozy) and Protocol 2 (Hermes/Orion) support, with standard openHPSDR UDP discovery
- Multiple simultaneous receivers, each with its own VFO, mode, filter width, and band memory
- Spectrum/waterfall display with adjustable dB range, palette, and Click-to-Tune (CTUN)
- SSB/CW/AM/FM/digital modes, per-mode/per-band filter width and mode memory
- Noise blanker (NB/NB2), noise reduction (NR/NR2/NNR), and SNB, independently switchable
- AGC with selectable Off/Long/Slow/Medium/Fast modes
- TX: mic audio through WDSP's TXA chain, ALC, TX power/SWR meter with per-band PA calibration, and a Tune button
- PureSignal (PA linearization/predistortion), on both Protocol 1 and Protocol 2
- rigctl (Hamlib-compatible), TCI (WebSocket), and CAT (Kenwood TS-2000 emulation) control servers
- Dual VFO (VFO A/B) with Split -- transmit on VFO B while receiving on VFO A
- Selectable RX output / TX input audio devices, independent of the OS default
- Per-radio settings persistence, keyed by the radio's MAC address
- FPGA firmware upload and static IP configuration
Changes since v0.12.2.
New
- CAT on serial ports (Settings → Network → CAT): the Kenwood CAT commands can now also be served on up to three serial ports, for an amplifier, tuner or band decoder that follows the radio over a CAT cable, or a program that only talks to a COM port. For each port:
  - Port and Baud (4800-115200, 8N1, no handshaking). A port that can't be opened, or is unplugged, is tried again every 2 seconds, so an amplifier switched on later is picked up by itself.
  - Auto report: sends the frequency and mode when they change, for a device that only listens.
  - TX frequency (on by default): reports the frequency you transmit on (VFO B with Split or Duplex, plus XIT), so an amplifier is on the band you transmit on.
  - PTT out: raises RTS or DTR while transmitting, e.g. to key an amplifier.
  - PTT in: a footswitch or program on CTS or DSR keys the radio.
- TX Delay (Settings → TX): holds RF back for 0-1000 ms after keying, while the PTT output, relays and a serial port's PTT line switch at once, so an amplifier's relay has closed before power arrives. Speech, data-mode audio, Tune and CW sent by hpsdr-rs start after the delay rather than being cut off.
- CAT auto-reporting (AI1/AI2) now works on the network CAT server too: frequency, and with AI2 mode, are sent when they change.
- MIDI (Settings → MIDI), from #15:
  - CW Key: a button or keyer bound to it keys CW from hpsdr-rs, keeping the key's timing.
  - New knob actions: CW Sidetone Level, CW Sidetone Frequency and CW Pitch.
  - Reverse for wheel controls, for an encoder that counts the wrong way.
  - Send changes back to the device (off by default): when a value bound to a knob changes in hpsdr-rs, the controller is sent its new position, so motor faders, LED rings or a keyer with its own display stay in step.
Changes
- The Stop button is now at the top of the main window, under Settings... and Add Receiver.
- At a reduced UI Scale the main and extra receiver windows can now be made smaller, in step with the scale. With the waterfall off, the spectrum can be made shorter too.
- ANAN-10E/100B: Add Receiver now offers the 2 receivers these radios have (it offered 5), and the PureSignal tab isn't shown: their PureSignal feedback can't go on receivers 3 and 4 as it does on other Hermes radios. Hermes and ANAN-10/100 now offer 4 receivers, the number their firmware has.
Fixes
- A gap under the Zoom/Pan sliders at the bottom of the window.
Downloads
- Linux AppImage (x86_64 / aarch64): hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-x86_64.AppImage, hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-aarch64.AppImage. Run chmod +x on the file, then run it. USB radios still need the udev rules installed by hand; a copy is inside the AppImage under usr/share/doc/hpsdr-rs.
- Debian/Ubuntu (amd64): hpsdr-rs_0.13.0-1_amd64.deb. Install with sudo apt install ./hpsdr-rs_0.13.0-1_amd64.deb.
- Debian/Ubuntu/Raspberry Pi OS (arm64): hpsdr-rs_0.13.0-1_arm64.deb. Install with sudo apt install ./hpsdr-rs_0.13.0-1_arm64.deb.
- Fedora/openSUSE RPM (x86_64 / aarch64): hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-1.x86_64.rpm, hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-1.aarch64.rpm. Install with sudo dnf install ./hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-1.x86_64.rpm, or on openSUSE sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-1.x86_64.rpm.
- macOS (Apple Silicon): hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz. It is built in CI, unsigned and not notarized, so Gatekeeper warns on first launch. Right-click the hpsdr-rs binary and choose Open, or run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine hpsdr-rs first.
- Windows (x86_64): hpsdr-rs-0.13.0-x86_64.msi
